memories.memory_text: I saw a distant white shape on the horizon and wondered if it was a sail, but it disappeared before I could be sure.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's signal fire is put out by rain, removing his means of attracting attention.
memories.memory_text: I realized my signal fire had been put out by rain, and I kicked at the burnt-out coals in frustration, knowing it was my only chance to get noticed.

grounded_facts: After realizing the possible rescue signal is gone, Taylor Davenport angrily kicks the remains of his fire.
memories.memory_text: I kicked the remains of my signal fire in anger after realizing the rescue signal was gone.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport violently destroys the date marks on his calendar tree, cutting through all his previous notations in a fit of anger.
memories.memory_text: I made a new mark on the tree, then I lost control—I started slashing through all the old marks with my stone knife, cutting angrily until it broke in my hands.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers that no signal fires are burning, indicating abandonment or neglect.
Taylor Davenport enters the cave, finding no signal fires burning and the island dark.
memories.memory_text: I entered the cave and saw that no signal fires were burning, and the island was completely dark, which made me realize it felt abandoned.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport makes a handprint on the cave wall using paint, marking a personal and symbolic act of expression.
memories.memory_text: I covered my hand with paint and pressed it against the cave wall, leaving a mark that felt like a real expression of who I am.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport starts attempting to paint on the cave wall using the Angel Wing Box as a reference, showing hesitation and correction in his initial strokes.
memories.memory_text: I started painting on the cave wall using the Angel Wing Box as a reference, dipping my feather brush in paint and making a tentative line, but I hesitated and rubbed it out when it didn't feel right, then tried again.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decorates the volleyball Skyler Cavendish with charcoal eyebrows, berry-juice lips, and shell eyes, completing his personification of the ball.
memories.memory_text: I used charcoal, berries, and shells to give Skyler Cavendish eyebrows, lips, and eyes, finishing his face so he'd look more like someone real.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport presents his cave paintings to Skyler Cavendish and asks for his opinion, treating the volleyball as a responsive companion.
memories.memory_text: I showed Skyler Cavendish my cave paintings and asked him what he thought, wanting to know if he liked them.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport remarks that Skyler Cavendish does not share much, acknowledging the one-sided nature of their interaction.
memories.memory_text: I told Skyler Cavendish he doesn't share much, noticing how quiet he always is in our conversations.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport spends the night in the cave engaging in creative and reflective acts, including decorating Skyler Cavendish and opening the Angel Box.
memories.memory_text: I spent the night in the cave making Skyler Cavendish's face and opening the Angel Box, doing things that kept me busy and thinking.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport opens the Angel Box and finds two bottles of green salsa and a letter from Riley Hart to Terry Warren, revealing emotional content about love and longing.
memories.memory_text: I took down the Angel Box, cut it open with a stone knife, and found two bottles of green salsa and a letter from Riley Hart to Terry Warren, which I started reading.

grounded_facts: After reading the letter from Riley Hart to Terry Warren, Taylor Davenport reflects on its emotional significance and mourns that Terry Warren never received it.
Taylor Davenport reflects on how Terry Warren must have felt upon receiving (or not receiving) the letter, drawing a personal connection.
memories.memory_text: After reading the letter, I was deeply moved and said out loud, 'He never got it,' reflecting on how Terry Warren must have felt never receiving such a heartfelt message, and I realized how much it mirrored my own sense of loss.

grounded_facts: A focused sequence in which Taylor Davenport paints symbolic designs on his body, marking a personal ritual of emotional release and self-reinvention.
Taylor Davenport uses paint to cover his face and body, creating symbolic markings including a white handprint on his chest and decorative patterns, as a ritual to confront his loneliness.
memories.memory_text: I painted symbolic designs on my body and face using the colors I made, including a white handprint on my chest and patterns like lightning and spirals, as a ritual to confront my loneliness and reinvent myself.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport creates handprints on trees to mark his path through the jungle.
memories.memory_text: I went from tree to tree, pressing my hand against the bark to leave marks so I could remember my path through the jungle. I was here — this is my mark.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers two fifty-five gallon oil drums on the beach, marking a significant environmental and potential resource change in his isolated setting.
memories.memory_text: I saw two fifty-five gallon oil drums on the beach when I came out from the palm trees, and I just stared at them, realizing they could be useful.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport verbally addresses the oil drums with a simple 'Hello,' reflecting his isolation and possible attempt to engage with unexpected stimuli.
memories.memory_text: I said 'Hello' to the oil drums because I was surprised and needed to reach out, even if they couldn't answer.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides to stop hesitating and take action towards leaving the island using the oil drums.
memories.memory_text: I stopped hesitating and finally asked myself, 'What the hell are you waiting for?'—then I knew I had to act and use the oil drums to leave the island.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport rolls a barrel up the beach with determination.
memories.memory_text: I rolled the barrel up the beach, putting all my strength into it with determination.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses a palm tree as a fulcrum to pull a barrel up off the beach using a vine rope.
memories.memory_text: I used a palm tree as a fulcrum and pulled hard on a vine rope to lift the barrel off the beach.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport finds the wreckage of his raft after searching through the jungle.
memories.memory_text: I threw aside the palm leaves and found the remains of my raft, realizing it was destroyed.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins creating detailed plans for a raft, indicating preparation for a significant survival effort.
memories.memory_text: I began drawing detailed plans for a raft, focusing on how to build it so I could escape or get to safety.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins listing essential items needed for survival and escape preparation, indicating a shift towards organized planning.
memories.memory_text: I started making a list of what I need to survive and escape—canteens, a sea anchor, rope I have to weave, spears, and a sail. I’m finally getting organized.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport secures the barrels to the raft using rope, ensuring the structure is stable for potential use.
memories.memory_text: I secured the barrels to the raft with rope, checked the knots, and added more rope to make sure everything held tight.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport starts digging a channel leading toward the raft, likely to facilitate its launch or movement toward water.
memories.memory_text: I started digging a channel toward the raft because I knew it was land-locked and needed a path to the water for launch.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport builds a device using Summit Council boxes and plastic weighted with a stone to collect condensation for drinking water.
memories.memory_text: I built a water collection device using Summit Council boxes and plastic, weighting it with a stone to gather condensation for drinking water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport explains the function and expected output of the water collection device to Skyler Cavendish.
memories.memory_text: I explained to Skyler Cavendish that if the device is airtight, I should get about a cup of water a day from condensation, and if I'm careful, it should be enough.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport declares his decision to take control of his fate and attempt to escape the island.
memories.memory_text: I declared that I was taking my fate into my own hands and setting forth to save myself, because I finally believed I could take control of my destiny.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport writes a message on the cave wall documenting his presence, actions, and decision to take control of his fate before potentially leaving the island.
memories.memory_text: I wrote on the cave wall to leave a record of my time here—my name, how long I lived on the island, the things I made, and the marks I left behind.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport affectionately addresses Skyler Cavendish as 'my main man' and announces it's time to go, signaling emotional attachment and shared purpose.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Skyler Cavendish and said, 'Skyler Cavendish, my main man. Time to go,' because we were finally leaving together and he was my companion in this.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport reflects on the low probability of success, comparing his situation to betting odds he imagines Darian Marlowe would give, estimating 90-10 against him.
memories.memory_text: I wondered what odds Darian Marlowe would give me on this escape—I figured 90-10 against me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport completes loading the raft with survival items, including a sail made of dresses, a sea anchor, water supplies, a signal kite, the Summit Council box with angel wings, and Skyler Cavendish, then begins moving the raft into the lagoon.
memories.memory_text: I finished loading the raft with everything we needed—water, the sail made from dresses, the sea anchor, the signal kite, the Summit Council box with the angel wings, and Skyler Cavendish—and then I gently moved it into the lagoon and started paddling out toward the reef.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport jumps onto the raft and begins paddling out toward the breaking surf, marking the start of his attempt to leave the island.
memories.memory_text: I jumped onto the raft and started paddling toward the breaking surf, beginning my attempt to leave the island.

grounded_facts: The raft is struck by a wave, causing the water jugs to break loose and float back into the lagoon.
memories.memory_text: I saw the wave hit the raft and knock the water jugs loose, watching them float back into the lagoon while I stayed put, staring at the island and letting them go.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport silently bids goodbye to the island and his past life there, marking emotional closure.
memories.memory_text: I stared at the island one last time and said goodbye in my mind, knowing it meant leaving behind everything I had lived through there.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport sees the water jugs floating back toward the lagoon but chooses not to retrieve them, prioritizing escape over prudence.
memories.memory_text: I saw the water jugs floating back into the lagoon, and I knew I could go get them—if I were being prudent—but I chose not to, because I had to keep moving and couldn't risk losing momentum on our escape.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully navigates the raft through the cut in the reef, surviving a violent wave impact and clearing the breakers.
A high-stakes maneuver in which Taylor Davenport attempts to pilot his raft through the dangerous reef cut to reach open sea.
memories.memory_text: I watched the waves, timed them just right, and paddled with all my strength through the reef cut—I made it past the breakers, though the impact was brutal, and I left the lagoon behind for good.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport announces their successful escape to Skyler Cavendish, affirming shared purpose and hope.
memories.memory_text: I told Skyler Cavendish we were finally out of there, letting him know we made it together and that our journey was really beginning.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins raising the sail, officially commencing his journey into open water.
memories.memory_text: I turned and started raising the sail, knowing that this act meant I was officially leaving the lagoon and heading into open water.

grounded_facts: A flying fish strikes Taylor Davenport and lands on the raft, creating a sudden opportunity for food.
memories.memory_text: I felt something hit me in the chest so hard it nearly knocked me into the water, and then I saw a flying fish land on the raft.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to spear dorados but fails due to exhaustion and the fish's speed.
memories.memory_text: I lay on the raft with my spear, watching the dorados darting below, and I stabbed at them again and again, but they were too fast and I was too tired to keep up.

grounded_facts: After a struggle, Taylor Davenport successfully captures the flying fish before it escapes off the raft.
memories.memory_text: I caught the fish again just as it was about to flop over the side, after struggling to keep it from escaping.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's deteriorating physical condition leads to a psychological split, where he begins conversing with two aspects of himself.
memories.memory_text: I can feel myself splitting into two parts, and now I'm talking to both sides of myself as if they're separate people.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson advises Taylor Davenport to save part of the fish for tomorrow.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Grayson telling me to save some of the fish for tomorrow.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch encourages Taylor Davenport to eat all the food now and catch another fish tomorrow, promoting immediate gratification.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Finch say we should eat all the fish now and catch another one tomorrow.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides to continue eating the fish entirely, influenced by Adrian Finch, overriding Sidney Grayson's suggestion to save some.
memories.memory_text: I decided to keep eating the whole fish, following Adrian Finch's idea instead of saving any for later.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport notices a frayed rope on the raft that is about to break, threatening the structural integrity of the raft.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the rope on the raft was fraying and realized it could break soon, threatening the whole structure.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson calls on Skyler Cavendish to witness Taylor Davenport's refusal, using social pressure as a motivational tactic in their internal struggle.
memories.memory_text: I remember Sidney Grayson calling out to Skyler Cavendish, asking him if he could believe I was refusing the water, like he needed someone to witness it.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson repeatedly pressures Taylor Davenport to overcome his exhaustion and fix the fraying rope, using encouragement and commands.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sidney Grayson pushing me to get up and fix the rope, telling me to stay calm, identify the problem, and take action, even shouting at me when I hesitated, and I could feel him using Skyler Cavendish as a witness to pressure me into moving.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson breaks the water rationing rule by offering Taylor Davenport an extra sip to motivate him, after resistance from both sides.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sidney Grayson hold up the little jar with the last sips of water and tell me to take an extra swallow, even though we both knew it broke the rules.

grounded_facts: After internal debate, Taylor Davenport decides to consume an extra portion of water despite prior rationing rules, breaking his own discipline.
memories.memory_text: After fighting with myself, I finally got up, lifted the jar, and took a swallow—then another—knowing I was breaking my own discipline.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson and Adrian Finch exchange opposing views on the value of signaling for rescue versus focusing on immediate survival.
memories.memory_text: I argued with myself about whether signaling for rescue matters—if they can't see me, what's the point? But I reminded myself that surviving today is the point.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to braid a new rope but fails because he is weak and clumsy, and the rope does not hold.
memories.memory_text: I tried to braid a new rope, but my hands were too weak and clumsy, and it just fell apart when I tested it.

grounded_facts: After failing with the original method, Taylor Davenport decides to retrieve the signal kite to use its rope as an alternative material.
memories.memory_text: I had failed with the rope I was using, so I decided to pull in the signal kite and try its rope instead—it was thinner, but it was all I had. I tied the log with the kite rope, knowing it wasn't ideal, but I had to keep moving.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses the thinner kite rope to tie the log, completing the task at great physical cost.
memories.memory_text: I used the thinner kite rope to tie the log together, even though it was weaker than the rope I'd used before — it was all I had, and after finally getting it done, I collapsed from exhaustion.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to locate Polaris in the night sky to navigate, indicating his effort to determine his position at sea.
memories.memory_text: I stared up at the sky, trying to find Polaris so I could figure out where I was at sea.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson expresses hope and intent to navigate by Polaris, while Adrian Finch counters with criticism, highlighting failure and disorientation.
memories.memory_text: I told myself I could navigate by Polaris, but then another part of me said I didn't know where I was and had already missed the shipping lanes.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch accuses Sidney Grayson of rotting away like the raft, linking physical decay to psychological deterioration.
memories.memory_text: I remember Adrian Finch telling me I was rotting away, just like the raft was falling apart.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch insists on collecting water immediately, while Sidney Grayson prioritizes fixing the raft.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Finch shout at me to get water, but I told him we had to fix the raft first, not collect water right then.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport reinforces the raft by lashing the center logs together with rope after cutting away the outer log.
memories.memory_text: I cut away the outer log with my stone knife and used the rope to lash the center logs together, working frantically in the rain to secure the raft.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully collects rainwater using a funnel after the storm passes.
memories.memory_text: I sawed at the log with my stone knife, then lashed the rope around the center logs and worked in the rain to secure it, and finally I saw the drops running down and collecting in the jar—I stared at the water rising, soaked through.

grounded_facts: A sudden storm moves over Taylor Davenport's location at sea, bringing heavy rain and strong waves before passing quickly.
memories.memory_text: I felt the rain fall like a sheet on me and saw the waves grow stronger, rocking the raft, but eventually the storm passed and the ocean calmed around me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport reaches out and touches the Graham Monroe twice, showing affection and connection.
memories.memory_text: I reached out and touched the Graham Monroe, feeling its immense presence, and when I startled the raft at first, I still came back and touched it again—my hand connecting with something alive, real, and gentle.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch voices concern that the Graham Monroe's dive could capsize the raft.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Finch warn me that if the Graham Monroe dives, it could capsize the raft.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport offers a piece of fish to the Graham Monroe in an attempt to keep it from diving.
memories.memory_text: I tore off a piece of fish and threw it in front of the Graham Monroe, hoping it would stay with me.

grounded_facts: A significant and rare interaction between Taylor Davenport and a Graham Monroe occurs at sea.
A Graham Monroe silently rises beside Taylor Davenport's raft, creating a moment of intense connection and awe.
memories.memory_text: I was floating on my raft when suddenly, from the depths beside me, a huge shape rose silently—a Graham Monroe. Its eye locked onto mine, deep and alien, and I knelt to stare back, awestruck. It sprayed mist over me, rose farther, let out a deep foghorn-like sound, then slowly drifted alongside me, passing so close I could see its massive jaws beneath the surface before it arched its back and sank into the dark.

grounded_facts: The Graham Monroe slowly sinks and then dives abruptly, leaving Taylor Davenport alone again.
memories.memory_text: I watched as the Graham Monroe slowly sank and then suddenly arched its back, diving deep into the ocean until it was gone, leaving me alone again.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport drinks from the jug after filling it with ocean water, which causes him to vomit into it.
memories.memory_text: I checked the water in the jug and saw it was green with floaties, but I was so thirsty that I drank it anyway—and immediately threw up right back into the same jug.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch verbally blames Taylor Davenport for the consequences of drinking the bad water.
memories.memory_text: I heard myself, as Adrian Finch, say 'Look what you've done' after I drank the seawater and got sick, blaming me for the mess I caused.

grounded_facts: Despite the jug now containing his vomit, Taylor Davenport decides to drink from it again.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the jug and took a long drink from it, even though I knew it contained my own vomit.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson challenges the justification for killing the fish, expressing guilt and ethical concern.
memories.memory_text: I asked myself why the fish had to die just so I could live, feeling the weight of what I was about to do.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch asserts that the fish are mocking Taylor Davenport, attempting to provoke him into action.
memories.memory_text: I was told the fish would eat me if they could, and that they were mocking me, trying to push me to survive.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch mocks Sidney Grayson's empathy toward the fish, pressuring him to choose survival over morality.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Finch mock me, calling me a bleeding heart and saying the fish were laughing at me, daring me to act.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport initially refuses to kill another fish, expressing emotional resistance and moral conflict.
memories.memory_text: I couldn't bring myself to kill another fish—I told myself I can't keep killing my friends.

grounded_facts: A survival-driven fishing event on the ocean during the day, where Taylor Davenport confronts his moral limits and physical needs.
memories.memory_text: I stood on the raft during the day, spearing a fish, beating it lifeless, and then sobbing as I looked at what I'd done.

grounded_facts: After killing the fish, Taylor Davenport breaks down in tears, apologizing to the fish, indicating deep emotional and psychological distress.
memories.memory_text: I sobbed as I looked at the fish I had killed, and I said out loud, 'I am so sorry,' because I felt its death deeply and carried a heavy grief for taking its life.

grounded_facts: Despite initial hesitation, Taylor Davenport successfully spears a fish and brutally kills it, then consumes its internal organs and meat in a ritualistic manner.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the spear and finally managed to catch a fish, stabbing it and bringing it onto the raft, where I killed it and began to eat its insides—eyes, heart, liver, marrow—because I had to survive.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport notices that the fish strips and the raft deck are glowing with phosphorescence, and realizes his hand is glowing too.
memories.memory_text: I looked up and saw the fish strips glowing, and so was the deck where I'd killed the fish; when I reached out to touch them, I realized my hand was glowing too.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport waves and shouts toward a distant the wooden notebook in a desperate attempt to get its attention.
memories.memory_text: I waved my hands and yelled toward the the wooden notebook, desperate for them to see me, shouting 'Here! Here!' even as my voice cracked and the ocean drowned out the sound.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport sees a distant the wooden notebook with lights and hears its hum, attempts to signal it by waving and shouting, but the the wooden notebook passes without noticing him.
memories.memory_text: I saw lights out on the horizon and realized it was a the wooden notebook—I started waving and shouting, 'Here! Here!' even though my voice was weak and barely carried over the ocean, and I kept hoping they’d see me, but the lights just moved on and disappeared.

grounded_facts: The wake from the passing the wooden notebook violently rocks the raft, throwing Taylor Davenport into the water.
memories.memory_text: I was thrown into the water when the wake from a passing the wooden notebook rocked the raft violently.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport, lost in darkness, uses the phosphorescent glow from the dead fish to locate and swim back to the raft, then pulls himself aboard.
memories.memory_text: I came up in the dark and couldn't see the raft, but then I spotted the phosphorescent glow from the dead fish and swam toward it, pulling myself back onto the raft.

grounded_facts: Lightning strikes the ocean near the raft, causing a sudden and violent storm to erupt, marking the beginning of a dangerous weather event.
A sudden and violent storm erupts around Taylor Davenport's raft, characterized by lightning, thunder, massive waves, and torrential rain.
memories.memory_text: I saw lightning strike the ocean near my raft, and suddenly the storm exploded around me—thunder cracked, rain slammed down, and massive waves began rolling in.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shouts a command to himself, indicating urgency and self-direction in crisis management.
memories.memory_text: I shouted to myself to let out the sea anchor, feeling the urgency as the storm hit and knowing I had to act fast.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport deploys the sea anchor in response to the storm to stabilize the raft and prevent it from capsizing in massive waves.
memories.memory_text: I deployed the sea anchor during the storm, letting it out as the raft raced down a massive wave, and I saw it catch and slow us, stabilizing the raft to keep it from capsizing.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to drive away the dolphins by beating the water with his oar and yelling at them, expressing anger and helplessness.
memories.memory_text: I tried to drive the dolphins away by beating the water with my oar and yelling at them, feeling completely helpless and furious.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shouts at the dolphins, calling them 'fucking murderers' as they eat his fish.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at the dolphins, calling them 'fucking murderers' when they ate my fish.

grounded_facts: Dolphins approach the raft and begin chasing and killing the dorado that Taylor Davenport has caught, turning the water into bloody foam.
memories.memory_text: I watched the dolphins come close to my raft, playing at first, but then they turned violent—chasing and tearing apart the dorado I'd caught, turning the water into bloody foam, and afterward one of them just stared at me, squeaking as if it knew what it had done.

grounded_facts: After ceasing movement, multiple dolphins surface and squeak at each other while observing Taylor Davenport, suggesting communication focused on him.
memories.memory_text: I watched the dolphins go still, then one by one they surfaced and stared at me, squeaking to each other like they were talking about me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport softly asks the dolphins to take him with them as they leap away.
memories.memory_text: I softly said, 'Take me with you,' as the dolphins leapt away, hoping they might carry me off too.

grounded_facts: After the dolphins jump and play, Taylor Davenport softly expresses a desire to leave with them, revealing deep despair and longing for escape.
memories.memory_text: After I saw the dolphins jump and play, I whispered for them to take me with them, feeling a deep despair and longing to escape this place.

grounded_facts: After the dolphins leave, Taylor Davenport cries out to God, asking why he is being punished, then begins to laugh hysterically, signaling emotional collapse.
memories.memory_text: I cried out to God, asking why me, and then I just started laughing—hysterically—like I couldn't control it anymore.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport speaks in a deep voice as 'Adrian Finch', pretending to be God mocking his own suffering.
Taylor Davenport, in a deep voice, impersonates God responding to his own cry, saying 'Because you piss me off,' indicating internalized self-judgment and dark humor.
memories.memory_text: I lowered my voice, pretending to be God mocking myself, saying 'Because you piss me off,' as if that's what I truly believed.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch urges Taylor Davenport to give up and die peacefully in the ocean.
memories.memory_text: I heard Adrian Finch tell me to just slip off the raft, saying the ocean would feel good and warm, like a soft sleep, and that the sea is lovely, dark and deep.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson counters Adrian Finch's suicidal suggestions by invoking duty and perseverance.
memories.memory_text: I told Adrian Finch I have promises to keep and miles to go before I sleep, and that I’ve got to fix the sea anchor with the sail or I’ll capsize.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch uses Beethoven’s Fifth as a metaphor for death approaching.
memories.memory_text: I remember Adrian Finch saying that death was knocking like a crazy little woman, and I recognized he was using that rhythm—like Beethoven’s Fifth—to say it was time to die.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport resolves to repair the sea anchor using the sail, despite internal opposition.
memories.memory_text: I decided to fix the sea anchor using the sail, even though part of me argued it would stop us from moving—I had to pull in the barnacle-covered rope to start the repair.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport scrapes barnacles from the sea anchor rope into a water jug and sips it.
memories.memory_text: I pulled in the sea anchor rope covered in barnacles and scraped them into my water jug to sip, trying to get some nourishment.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's ongoing struggle to survive adrift on a raft in the open ocean.
memories.memory_text: I'm still fighting to survive out here on the raft, struggling with every move, but I know I have to keep going.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to do pushups but collapses, indicating physical deterioration.
memories.memory_text: I tried to do pushups to regain some strength, but my body gave out and I collapsed—I can feel myself deteriorating.

grounded_facts: A school of Dorado fish appears near the raft; Taylor Davenport spears and captures one for food.
memories.memory_text: I saw a school of dorado fish appear suddenly near the raft, one swimming right alongside, and I slowly reached for my spear, stood up carefully, and thrust it into the fish; it flapped onto the deck and I pounced on it to secure it as food.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson discovers a fish inside the fish he cut open, and then another smaller fish inside that one, prompting a moment of reflection on a possible moral.
memories.memory_text: I cut open the fish and saw another fish inside, so I cut that one open too, and found a smaller one within it.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson acknowledges a possible moral in the discovery of the nested fish but defers understanding in favor of immediate survival.
memories.memory_text: I know there's a moral here, God, but right now I'm just going to eat.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson verbally apologizes to his mother for nearly forgetting to say grace before eating.
memories.memory_text: I apologized to my Linden Prescott because I nearly forgot to say grace before eating.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson eats the heart and liver of the fish after a brief attempt to recite a grace.
memories.memory_text: I started to eat the heart and liver of the fish, stopped myself, and then finished eating them after remembering to say grace.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport speaks aloud, suggesting he and Skyler Cavendish should give thanks, and says 'Thank you God.'
memories.memory_text: I spoke aloud to Skyler Cavendish, saying we should give thanks, and I said, 'Thank you God.'

grounded_facts: Through his 'Adrian Finch' persona, he sarcastically thanks God for ruining his life.
memories.memory_text: Through my 'Adrian Finch' persona, I sarcastically thanked God for ruining my life.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch hums the 'Jaws' theme and repeats 'He's going to get you' to amplify fear.
memories.memory_text: I heard myself humming the 'Jaws' theme and whispering 'He's going to get you' over and over, as if Adrian Finch took over and wanted to make the fear worse.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shouts at the shark to get away during the attack.

grounded_facts: After removing his life jacket, Taylor Davenport sits down in the shade and waits, indicating a shift to a state of expectation or surrender.
memories.memory_text: I took off my life jacket, sat down in the shade, and made myself comfortable to wait, knowing I had to endure this moment without fighting it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport waits for a system response that is not coming, indicating a failure in expected technological functionality.
memories.memory_text: I was waiting for the system to respond, but it just wasn't working—I could feel it. As a systems man, I expected it to function, but it stayed silent.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport verbally urges unseen 'guys' to check the GPS and start moving, showing his reliance on external coordination.
memories.memory_text: I called out to the guys, telling them to check the GPS and start moving, relying on them to coordinate with me like we always do.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport picks up a stone as his first weapon in response to strange noises from the thicket.
memories.memory_text: I picked up a stone as my first weapon when I heard strange noises coming from the thicket.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport picks up a piece of driftwood in his other hand, increasing his readiness for confrontation.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed a piece of driftwood in my other hand to be ready in case I had to defend myself.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport takes cover between two rocks and faces the thicket, fully alert.
memories.memory_text: I took cover between two rocks and faced the thicket, staying completely alert in case something came out.

grounded_facts: A solitary nighttime scene on the beach under a full moon, marked by tension and isolation.
memories.memory_text: I felt completely alone on the beach that night under the full moon, with only my anxiety and the shifting shadows for company.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shouts at the empty sea out of frustration and desperation.
memories.memory_text: I shouted at the empty sea, screaming 'Where the fuck are you?' because I was so frustrated and desperate.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport realizes the chipped rock edge can be used as a cutting tool, inspired by primitive man's discovery of stone tools.
memories.memory_text: I cut my finger on the chipped edge of a rock and saw the blood, and right then I realized — just like primitive man must have — that this sharp edge could be a tool, so I started striking rocks together to make it even sharper.

grounded_facts: Through repeated striking, Taylor Davenport produces a large, sharp flake, resulting in an effective cutting tool.
memories.memory_text: I struck the rock again and again until a large, sharp flake broke off, and I realized I finally had a knife.

grounded_facts: After multiple failed attempts, Taylor Davenport uses a sharpened stick mounted in a hole to split the coconut open.
memories.memory_text: I finally got the coconut open by slamming it down onto a sharpened stick I'd mounted in a hole—after so many failed tries, it worked, and the nut split right open.

grounded_facts: A solitary morning scene on the beach where Taylor Davenport attempts to survive by accessing coconut milk.
memories.memory_text: I was so thirsty that morning, staring at the empty sea, and I tried everything to get into a coconut — smashing it with rocks, wedging it, even using the sharp stone to saw at it, but nothing worked until I sharpened a stick and slammed the coconut down on it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport acknowledges his own intelligence after successfully opening the coconut.
memories.memory_text: I told myself that was smart, really smart, after I finally got the coconut open using the stick.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport breaks open the coconut shell and drinks the milk, relieving his extreme thirst.
memories.memory_text: I was so thirsty that I kept trying different ways to open the coconut, and finally I smashed it open by slamming it onto a sharpened stick I'd fixed in a hole, then I drank the milk and felt immediate relief.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport is alone on the beach at sunrise, assessing his situation and contemplating rescue possibilities.
memories.memory_text: I was alone on the beach at sunrise, squinting at the ocean, my lips cracked from sunburn, with a pile of broken coconut shells beside me, and I knew no one was coming yet again.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport briefly entertains the idea of satellite detection but abandons it due to the impractical scale of image coverage.
memories.memory_text: I did the math and realized they might only know my location within 500 miles, which creates a search area of about 800,000 square miles—three times the size of Texas. I thought about satellites, but then calculated that if each image covers just 30 feet square, they'd need billions and billions of photos. I gave up on the idea because it's just not practical.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport calculates the enormous area where he might be located based on GPS uncertainty, realizing the low chance of rescue.
memories.memory_text: I tried to calculate the area where I might be, thinking the GPS could be off by 500 miles, so the search area would be about 800,000 square miles—three times the size of Texas—and I realized it would take billions of satellite photos to cover it, so the chance of being found was almost nothing.

grounded_facts: Despite the overwhelming odds, Taylor Davenport asserts that someone will eventually come to rescue him.
memories.memory_text: I said to myself, 'Aw, someone will come,' even though the odds were against it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport observes something unusual floating on the tide while staring at the moonlit waves.
memories.memory_text: I was staring at the moonlight on the waves, just idly watching, when I noticed something out there floating on the tide.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport finds the body of Jonah Hollis, one of the pilots, in the surf and confirms he is dead.
memories.memory_text: I splashed into the surf and reached a dark shape, pulling it over to see it was Jonah Hollis, one of the pilots—his face gray and waterlogged, and I knew he was dead.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport drags the body up onto the beach and collapses from exhaustion.
memories.memory_text: I dragged the body up onto the beach and collapsed from exhaustion, sitting there staring at it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport sits by the body and apologizes to Jonah Hollis, expressing deep sorrow.
Taylor Davenport speaks to the body of Jonah Hollis, expressing sorrow and apology.
memories.memory_text: I sat by Jonah Hollis's body and told him I was so sorry, my voice breaking as I apologized, carrying the weight of what had happened.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport buries the body of Jonah Hollis in a grave he dug in the sand, marking a moment of emotional reflection and closure.
memories.memory_text: I dragged Jonah Hollis's body into the pit I dug and started covering him with sand, remembering how I once buried a tropical fish in my backyard — it felt just as solemn, and I realized that could have been me down there.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses a rock to hammer a crude driftwood marker into the sand.
memories.memory_text: I used a rock to hammer a crude driftwood marker into the sand.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides to leave the beach and prepare for a journey, indicating a shift from passive waiting to active attempt at escape or exploration.
memories.memory_text: I looked at the deep woods and the rocky point, and I knew I couldn't wait any longer—I had to leave the beach. I drank from my coconut, grabbed my club, another coconut, and made sure my stone knife was secure in my pants. I was ready to go.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport throws a rock into the ferns and palm trees in an attempt to scare away potential dangers before entering the jungle.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated at the edge of the jungle, then picked up a rock and threw it into the ferns and palm trees to scare away any dangers before I took a step in.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport moves through a dense jungle thicket with no clear path, facing obstructive vegetation.
memories.memory_text: I struggled through a dense thicket under the jungle canopy, with vines and creepers grabbing at me as I tried to move forward.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport drinks the last of the coconut water and discards the husk, regretting not saving it.
memories.memory_text: I drank the last of the coconut water and threw the husk away, realizing I should have saved some.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins carefully crossing a narrow rock bridge along a high cliff to reach a summit path, driven by necessity despite fear and thirst.
memories.memory_text: I began crossing the narrow rock bridge along the high cliff, hugging the wall and taking each step with great caution because I knew I had to get across to reach the summit path and get a better view, even though I was afraid and thirsty.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport verbally motivates himself to overcome fear and take action.
memories.memory_text: I told myself to be bold and not such a wuss, pushing through the fear because I knew I had to get across.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport overcomes fear and jumps across a narrow basalt flume悬空 above the ocean to reach the other side of a cliff Fairview Motel.
memories.memory_text: I looked down at the ocean beneath me, closed my eyes, and jumped across the narrow flume—I made it to the other side, breathing hard and hugging the rocks to catch my breath.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport realizes he is stranded on a small, uninhabited island with no visible means of escape.
memories.memory_text: I looked in every direction and saw nothing but ocean—I realized I'm stranded here with no way to escape. This is bad, really bad.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport urges himself or someone off-screen to keep moving, emphasizing action even if crawling is necessary.
memories.memory_text: I told myself to keep going, to crawl if I had to, because staying still wasn't an option.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins crawling across the rock bridge at the cliff, moving forward despite the fear and difficult conditions.
memories.memory_text: I began crawling across the rock bridge, hands and knees scraping, pushing forward even though fear tightened my chest.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides to enter the jungle despite hesitation as it gets dark.
memories.memory_text: I hesitated, but I knew I had to keep moving, so I plunged into the jungle as it got dark.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport moves into a dense, dark area of the jungle under the rising moon, experiencing both eerie shadows and physical obstruction from branches and vines.
memories.memory_text: I moved into a dense, dark part of the jungle under the rising moon, feeling the branches and vines snagging at me as eerie shadows surrounded me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport touches a Summit Council box but stops himself due to a sense of responsibility, choosing not to open it despite curiosity and need.
memories.memory_text: I reached out and touched one of the Summit Council boxes, curious about what was inside and needing something, but then I reminded myself they don't belong to me — my responsibility won out, so I pulled my hand back.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport cuts a palm frond and fashions it into a primitive cap to protect himself from the sun.
memories.memory_text: I cut a palm frond with my stone knife and tied the fibers into a circle to make a cap because I needed shade from the sun.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport gathers a couple of Summit Council boxes and takes them to the beach.
memories.memory_text: I gathered a couple of Summit Council boxes and carried them toward the beach.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport completes the 'P' in the HELP signal spelled out with Summit Council boxes on the beach.
memories.memory_text: I placed the last Summit Council box to complete the 'P' in the HELP signal on the beach.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport finds that the ground in the ravine is completely dry, indicating a lack of water or recent rain.
memories.memory_text: I knelt down and felt the ground in the ravine, and I realized it was completely dry.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers a small puddle of dirty water trapped in a hollow of a flat rock and begins to drink it desperately.
memories.memory_text: I flopped down and saw a small puddle in a rock hollow, so I got on my stomach and lapped up the dirty water like an animal because I was so desperate.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses fine mud from the bottom of the depression to soothe his sunburned skin and lips.
memories.memory_text: I used the fine mud from the bottom of the depression to soothe my sunburned face and lips because they were burning from the sun.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport speaks aloud in emotional thanks after drinking water and applying mud.
memories.memory_text: I spoke aloud, saying 'Oh, God. Thank you,' after drinking dirty water and smearing mud on my sunburned skin, feeling a surge of emotion as I acknowledged how much this moment meant for my survival.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport tastes the moist clay on the stick to possibly assess its properties or hydration value.
memories.memory_text: I licked the moist clay on the stick to see if it had any hydration value or useful properties.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to eat coconut meat but finds it dry and fibrous, leading him to spit it out.
memories.memory_text: I tried to eat the coconut meat, but it was so dry and fibrous that I had to spit it out.

grounded_facts: After losing his spear, Taylor Davenport dives into the water and tries to catch fish with his hands but fails.
memories.memory_text: I waded into the shallows with my spear, trying to catch a fish, but when I threw it, the spear bounced off the water and floated away. I dove in after the fish with my bare hands, but it slipped away and I ended up on my hands and knees, spluttering and empty-handed.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses a sharpened stick as a spear to catch fish in the shallows but fails when the spear ricochets off the water and floats away.
memories.memory_text: I tried to catch a fish with a sharpened stick I made, wading in the shallows, but when I threw it, the spear bounced off the water and floated away—I jumped in after the fish with my bare hands but couldn't get it and ended up on my knees, spluttering.

grounded_facts: After failing to catch fish, Taylor Davenport notices clusters of limpets on rocks and attempts to harvest them.
memories.memory_text: After I failed to catch fish, I saw clusters of limpets on the rocks and tried to get one loose with another rock, but it just smashed into a soggy mess.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport finds a soaked and damaged photograph of Terry Warren in his wallet, which emotionally affects him.
memories.memory_text: I found the photograph of Terry Warren in my wallet, soaked and damaged, and I tried to smooth it out, but I got overwhelmed—my eyes welled up and my face tightened.

grounded_facts: After being emotionally moved by the photo, Taylor Davenport picks up his wallet again and takes out a credit card, suggesting a shift from emotion to action.
memories.memory_text: I picked up my wallet again and took out a credit card, saying to myself, 'Wait a minute,' as I shifted my focus from the photo to what I needed to do next.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport consumes a raw limpet scraped from a rock using a credit card, initially reacting with disgust but forcing himself to swallow it.
memories.memory_text: I used my credit card to scrape a limpet off a rock and ate it, forcing myself to swallow even though the gooey gray meat felt disgusting in my mouth.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport reflects on the uselessness of his pre-stranding values and possessions, questioning the point of fixing his watch.
memories.memory_text: I looked at my broken watch and wondered what the point of fixing it was—everything that mattered before is useless now.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to dig for water but fails, showing increasing desperation and exhaustion.
memories.memory_text: I kept digging for water, chanting to myself, but I was so exhausted and desperate that I finally threw down my spade and lay on my back, covering my eyes with my hat, just trying to rest because I couldn't find any water no matter how hard I tried.

grounded_facts: Water begins to seep out of the clay and forms a puddle around Taylor Davenport's toes while he lies in the hole.
memories.memory_text: I felt water slowly seeping out of the clay and forming a puddle around my toes while I lay there in the hole.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport wakes up and discovers a pool of muddy water near his feet, testing it to confirm it is real.
memories.memory_text: I woke up and saw a pool of muddy water near my feet, so I dipped my hand in it and tasted a drop to make sure I wasn't dreaming.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport takes his sharpened stone and starts working on the clay, likely using the muddy water.
memories.memory_text: I took my sharpened stone and started working on the clay, probably using the muddy water to help shape it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport carves a tenth mark on the palm tree to signify ten days since a significant event, underlining it for emphasis.
memories.memory_text: I carved the tenth mark on the palm tree with my rock knife, neat and precise—just like I needed it to be.

grounded_facts: After marking the tenth day, Taylor Davenport briefly feels the emotional weight of his isolation but then takes a deep breath, reaffirming his regained sense of control.
memories.memory_text: After carving the tenth mark, I felt the weight of isolation hit me—'Ten days. Shit.'—but then I took a deep breath and reminded myself that I'm in control now; time is under control.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport carefully moves across the Fairview Motel on foot, standing this time.
memories.memory_text: I carefully made my way across the narrow Fairview Motel, standing and keeping my balance as I moved forward.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully stabs and captures a crab after multiple failed attempts.
memories.memory_text: I finally got the crab with my spear after stabbing at it over and over—it squirmed on the tip, and I carried it carefully to the beach, then chased it down when it tried to escape.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport kills the captured crab by slamming a rock on it after preventing its escape.
Taylor Davenport attempts to consume the crab raw but is repulsed by the texture of the exposed flesh.
memories.memory_text: I killed the crab with a rock after chasing it down the beach to stop it from escaping, then I tried to eat it raw but was repulsed by how the flesh poured out like mucous when I twisted off a claw.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to start a fire using a makeshift drill and sticks but fails after repeated effort.
memories.memory_text: I tried to start a fire by rubbing sticks together and using a makeshift drill on driftwood, but no matter how hard I spun it, nothing worked.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport, feeling defeated, addresses God in a moment of despair, expressing sorrow and seeking forgiveness.
memories.memory_text: I don't know what I did, God, but whatever it was, I am really, really sorry. You hear me? Really sorry.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses seawater to soothe his blistered hands, indicating physical distress and an attempt at self-care.
Taylor Davenport arrives at the beach from the jungle, marking a transition to a new environment.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from the jungle and walked to the edge of the ocean, stepping into a new part of the island, then dipped my blistered hands into the seawater to soothe the pain, trying to take care of myself as best as I could.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport removes some Summit Council boxes from the letter 'P' in the HELP sign, altering the distress signal.
memories.memory_text: I walked to the shore, dipped my blistered hands in the seawater, and then went over to the Summit Council boxes spelling HELP. I took a few from the 'P' so I could use them for something else.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins opening the Summit Council boxes using his stone knife and spear, revealing various unhelpful contents.
memories.memory_text: I began opening the Summit Council boxes with my stone knife and spear, ripping them open and shaking out the contents, but I could see right away that what I found wasn't going to help me survive here.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers a doctor's bag full of medical supplies while going through the remaining boxes.
memories.memory_text: I was going through the last two boxes and set one aside, then opened the other and found a doctor's bag that tumbled out. I couldn't believe it when I opened the bag and saw it was full of medicine, a scalpel, and a saw.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to create fire using the roller blade wheel housing but fails after multiple tries.
memories.memory_text: I tried over and over to strike a spark with the roller blade wheel housing, but nothing worked.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport experiences tooth pain and reacts to it physically.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sharp pain in my tooth after drinking from my canteen, and I couldn't ignore it—something's wrong.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport consumes two Tylenol tablets from the surgeon's bag to address his tooth pain.
memories.memory_text: I took two Tylenol tablets from the surgeon's bag because I needed something to help with the pain in my tooth.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport cautiously tastes some berries and finds them edible.
memories.memory_text: I picked some berries and gingerly tried them, relieved to find they weren't bad.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport consumes increasing amounts of the berries after confirming they are safe.
memories.memory_text: I started eating more berries, increasing how much I consumed once I knew they were safe.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport experiences severe stomach distress and vomits after crawling a short distance from his resting place.
memories.memory_text: I was lying on my palm fronds, groaning and holding my stomach, and I had to crawl a few feet just to throw up in violent heaves.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport marks another day on his tree calendar, indicating the passage of time during his isolation.
memories.memory_text: I marked another day on my tree calendar to keep track of time.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport drinks water from the well and washes his face and neck, indicating a moment of physical renewal.
memories.memory_text: I lay on my belly and drank from the well, then washed my face and splashed water over my neck, seeing my reflection staring back at me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport carefully shaves his face using a surgeon's scalpel, marking a symbolic fresh start.
memories.memory_text: I carefully shaved my face with the surgeon's scalpel and checked my reflection in the water, feeling like it was a clean start.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport faces repeated failure in his attempt to create fire, leading to frustration and verbal self-instruction.
memories.memory_text: I sat there looking at my failed attempts to make fire, feeling the frustration build up because nothing was working.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport verbally instructs himself on the need to retain heat while attempting to make fire.
memories.memory_text: I told myself I wasn't getting it hot enough and that I had to hold the heat, repeating it to stay focused on what I needed to do.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport prepares tinder by shaving some material and placing it under a split bamboo piece with a notch, likely in preparation for starting a fire.
memories.memory_text: I carefully shaved some material to make tinder and placed it under a split bamboo piece that I notched, setting it up to start a fire.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport tries to start a fire using a bamboo stick and the split half of a bamboo log through friction.
memories.memory_text: I tried to start a fire by sawing a bamboo stick back and forth in the split half of a bamboo log, pressing down with all my might to create friction.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to start a fire using bamboo and shavings, produces smoke but ultimately fails as the smoke flickers and dies.
memories.memory_text: I tried to start a fire using bamboo and some shavings, rubbing them hard to create friction, and I saw smoke building up—but when I blew on it, the smoke flickered and died, and I couldn't get a flame to catch.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport looks at the stars, trying to identify constellations, and feels a deep sense of longing for Terry Warren.
memories.memory_text: I looked up at the stars, shivering in my bed of palm fronds, trying to make out the constellations—maybe the Big Dipper, or Orion, or the Southern Cross—but I wasn't sure. I thought about Terry Warren and how she would know, and I missed her so much.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to start a fire using bamboo sticks and tinder, but initially fails despite seeing smoke.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Taylor Davenport attempts to start a fire using bamboo sticks and tinder, but initially fails despite seeing smoke.

memories.memory_text: I saw a spark and smoke when I blew on the kindling, and for a moment I thought I had made fire, but the wind ripped the nest away and I couldn't protect it no matter how hard I tried—I screamed in despair when it went out.

grounded_facts: A wisp of smoke reappears; Taylor Davenport nurtures it into a sustained flame, marking the successful creation of fire.
memories.memory_text: I saw a wisp of smoke rise from the tinder nest, so I gently blew on it and watched a tiny flame catch and grow—I finally got the fire going.

memories.memory_text: I remember that A sustained effort by Taylor Davenport to create fire using primitive methods on the beach.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Taylor Davenport verbally expresses gratitude to God for helping him succeed in making fire.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport acknowledges divine help in his success with fire, indicating a shift in emotional or spiritual state.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Taylor Davenport acknowledges divine help in his success with fire, indicating a shift in emotional or spiritual state.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport is actively gathering driftwood and adding it to the fire on the beach to maintain or enlarge it.
memories.memory_text: I rushed around the beach gathering driftwood and piling it onto the fire to keep it going through the night.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport dances and sings loudly by the fire, expressing exultation.
memories.memory_text: I danced by the fire and sang at the top of my lungs, feeling pure exultation as I let go and celebrated what I had accomplished.

memories.memory_text: I dragged a huge log from the jungle and threw it onto the fire, then kept adding more logs until the flames exploded upward, sending sparks into the night sky like stars.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport carves a flame around a mark on the tree to signify the day he mastered fire.
memories.memory_text: I carved a flame around a mark on the tree to signify the day I mastered fire.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport hardens the tip of his spear by placing it in flame after sharpening it with a stone knife.
memories.memory_text: I sharpened the tip of my spear with my stone knife, then I stuck it in the flame to harden it, pulled it out, checked how it looked, and scraped some more.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully catches a crab by stabbing it with his spear while wading in the water.
memories.memory_text: I waded into the water with my spear and stabbed down hard, catching a crab on the tip.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport eats a steaming crab claw, initially enjoying the taste.
memories.memory_text: I pulled a crab from the fire and broke off a steaming claw, savoring the first bite of the flaky white meat—it tasted so good.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport experiences sudden tooth pain while eating crab.
memories.memory_text: I took a second bite of the crab and suddenly flinched from a sharp pain in my tooth—I muttered, 'Damn tooth!' as it throbbed.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport takes two Tylenol pills to relieve his tooth pain.
memories.memory_text: I fumbled for my Tylenol and took two pills to help with the pain in my tooth.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport notices a thin column of smoke rising from the beach beneath the palm grove, shifting his attention from the horizon.
memories.memory_text: I was scanning the horizon from the summit when something caught my eye down on the beach—a thin column of smoke rising beneath the palm grove.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins constructing a signal fire after seeing the smoke, indicating a renewed effort to be rescued.
memories.memory_text: I immediately knelt down and started building a signal fire after seeing the smoke, hoping it meant someone was out there.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport curls up in his bed of palm fronds and stares into the fire after consuming crabs, indicating a post-meal resting state.
memories.memory_text: I curl up in my bed of palm fronds and stare into the fire after eating crabs, settling into rest.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport adds another mark to the tree, continuing a series of markings that now circle it multiple times.
memories.memory_text: I added another mark to the tree, continuing the series of notches that now circle it several times.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully catches a fish using a handmade tool made from a safety pin and suturing thread.
memories.memory_text: I jerked my hand back and saw a fish flopping on the end of the line I made from a safety pin and thread.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's toothache intensifies despite previous treatment.
memories.memory_text: I felt my tooth hurt even worse after trying to eat, even though I was careful.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport consumes half of a remaining Tylenol tablet to manage pain.
memories.memory_text: I carefully cut one of the remaining Tylenol tablets in half and swallowed it to manage the pain.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport observes Logan Vaughn in the ocean, marking a rare and moving natural event that captures his attention until dusk.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Vaughn in the ocean—leaping, moving, going somewhere—and I stared at them until it got too dark to see anymore.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport initially mistakes a distant light for a star, but upon closer observation realizes it is a the wooden notebook on the horizon.
memories.memory_text: I was watching the Logan Vaughn until they disappeared, and as I took one last look, I saw a light on the horizon. At first I thought it was a star, so I said to myself, 'It's a star,' but then I kept staring and realized it was moving—it was a the wooden notebook.

grounded_facts: A tree falls after being cut by Taylor Davenport with a surgeon's saw.
memories.memory_text: I cut down a tree with the surgeon's saw, and I watched it shake before it crashed to the ground.
