memories.memory_text: I finished building the raft using logs, vines, bamboo, and driftwood I'd gathered over time—I sewed dresses into a sail, cut bamboo for the mast, carved an oar from driftwood, filled gourds with water, stored breadfruit and coconuts, and tied everything together with palm fiber and tape, even securing the doctor's kit and the Summit Council box with angel wings before stepping back to look at what I'd made.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to pull and push the raft to the water but fails due to its weight, leading to physical exhaustion and emotional frustration.
memories.memory_text: I tried to pull and push the raft to the water, but it wouldn't move no matter how hard I strained—it was too heavy, and I collapsed on the beach, gasping for breath.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport expresses intense self-criticism after realizing a critical flaw in his plan, likely the raft's inability to be moved to the water.
memories.memory_text: I tried to pull the raft to the water, but it wouldn't move no matter how hard I pushed or pulled, and I just collapsed on the beach, breathing hard. I kept asking myself how I could have been so stupid, banging my head and calling myself stupid over and over.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport gets an idea after watching a wave carry away a coconut husk.
memories.memory_text: I watched a wave carry away a coconut husk and suddenly got an idea about how ocean currents might help me escape.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport collapses in despair after failing to escape, sobs, and releases a primal scream that seems to trigger environmental changes.
memories.memory_text: I swam back to shore after another failed escape, threw the Summit Council box down, ripped off my life preserver, and collapsed—completely broken. I couldn't hold it in anymore, so I sobbed, then screamed into the sky with everything I had, a raw cry of rage and pain that cut through the island's silence.

grounded_facts: A sudden and intense downpour begins, threatening Taylor Davenport's fire and forcing immediate action.
memories.memory_text: I felt the first drops of rain sizzle in the fire, and when I looked up, the sky had darkened with heavy clouds — then the monsoon hit, pouring down in sheets, threatening to drown my fire completely.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport rescues burning coals from the fire before it is extinguished by rain, using a Summit Council box to transport them.
memories.memory_text: I grabbed an empty Summit Council box and used my shovel to scoop up burning coals before the rain could extinguish them, then carried them away with some driftwood to keep the fire alive.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport is running through the woods while struggling with difficult terrain and heavy rain.
memories.memory_text: I was running through the woods, slipping and struggling as the heavy rain made it hard to see, and vines kept grabbing at me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport exits the woods and enters the lava field, carrying the smoking Summit Council package.
The Summit Council package carried by Taylor Davenport is smoking and close to burning through due to hot coals inside.
memories.memory_text: I burst out of the woods into the lava field, carrying the smoking Summit Council package—I could see the smoke pouring out and knew the hot coals inside were about to burn through it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport drags a smoking box across slippery rocks in a desperate attempt to move it.
memories.memory_text: I dragged the smoking box across the slippery rocks, struggling with every step because I knew I had to get it moved right away.

grounded_facts: The coals from the Summit Council box go out one by one due to rain and lack of dry fuel, nearly ending Taylor Davenport's attempt to restart the fire.
memories.memory_text: I watched helplessly as the precious coals from the Summit Council box went out one by one in the rain, and I knew my chance to restart the fire was slipping away.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully restarts a small flame by adding kindling and fanning the coals with the remains of the box.
memories.memory_text: I stomped on the driftwood and cut it with my knife to make kindling, then placed it on the coals and fanned them with the remains of the box until a small flame caught and started to grow.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport ventures into the storm to collect more firewood, risking injury and exposure.
memories.memory_text: I ventured into the storm to gather more firewood, even though I could barely see and the waves were closing in.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport is trapped in the cave at night, unable to escape due to darkness, rain, and physical pain from his toothache.
memories.memory_text: I'm lying in the cave, shivering in the dark while the rain keeps falling, my fire is out, and my tooth is killing me—I can't move or escape like this.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport exits the cave, facing the aftermath of the storm and his failed survival efforts.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from the cave and saw the destruction left by the storm, realizing how much I had lost.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport confronts the complete collapse of his survival progress and feels hopeless.
memories.memory_text: I felt overwhelming despair as I faced the ruin of everything I had worked for, and I wasn't sure I could go on.

grounded_facts: After nearly falling, Taylor Davenport consciously chooses to fight for survival instead of ending his life.
memories.memory_text: I had wanted to end it, come so close—but my deepest instinct was to survive. And that is what I am going to do.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport questions his own actions and then affirms his decision to survive.
memories.memory_text: I walked out on the Fairview Motel, slid one foot to the very edge, and realized I had come so close to ending it all. I asked myself, 'What the fuck are you doing?' and then told myself, 'Hang on. Just hang on.'

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's foot slips while he is balancing on the edge of the precipice, triggering a moment of physical crisis.
memories.memory_text: I was walking along the Fairview Motel and staring down at the waves below when my foot slipped, and I instinctively grabbed the cliff face to keep from falling.

grounded_facts: A solitary moment on the Fairview Motel where Taylor Davenport faces his will to die and ultimately chooses survival.
memories.memory_text: In that moment, I wasn't sure if I wanted to keep going, but I felt something inside push me to fight—I chose to pull myself back instead of letting go.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers a soccer ball washed up on the beach, which he later names Skyler Cavendish, marking the beginning of a significant emotional connection.
memories.memory_text: I saw a soccer ball washed up on the beach with 'Skyler Cavendish' stamped on it, so I picked it up, kicked it, and ran after it to keep it from the water—I felt joy again, even here.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport consumes the last half tablet of Tylenol, marking the depletion of his pain relief medication.
memories.memory_text: I took the last half tablet of Tylenol with a sip from my coconut canteen, knowing I had no more pain relief left.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport experiences intensified tooth pain when consuming coconut meat and water, indicating a deteriorating dental condition.
memories.memory_text: I felt a sharp pain in my tooth when I bit into the coconut meat, and it hurt again when I drank the water — I realized eating and drinking were making it worse.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to treat his toothache using a mixture of breadfruit and coconut, but the sensitivity causes pain.
memories.memory_text: I tried to treat my toothache by mixing breadfruit and coconut and packing it into the sore tooth, but it hurt too much because the tooth was so sensitive.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport pounds the cave floor in response to the pain from his failed dental treatment.
memories.memory_text: I pounded the cave floor with my fists because the pain from my failed treatment made me so frustrated.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport prepares to use a stone chisel on his inflamed tooth but stops due to fear.
memories.memory_text: I held the stone chisel against my inflamed tooth, ready to knock it out, but the fear of what I was about to do made me lower it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to drink seawater to cope with pain, which causes him further distress.
memories.memory_text: I tried to drink seawater to ease the pain, but it only made things worse and my eyes started watering from the agony.

grounded_facts: After failing to drink seawater, Taylor Davenport falls back and floats, looking at the sky.
memories.memory_text: After I failed to drink the seawater, I fell back and floated in the water, looking up at the sky.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport picks up the stone chisel and hammer stone with determination, then strikes the chisel in an effort to create or modify something, enduring intense pain.
memories.memory_text: I picked up the stone chisel and hammer with determination, raised the chisel to my mouth, and brought the hammer down hard—I told myself no pain, no gain, but the pain was immediate and overwhelming as I screamed into the blackness.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully spears a fish in the morning light, demonstrating his adapted survival skills.
memories.memory_text: I saw the fish and swiftly speared it with my handmade tool, pulling it out with a practiced twist—I’ve gotten good at this.

grounded_facts: A routine fishing activity carried out by Taylor Davenport at sunrise on the island's cove.
memories.memory_text: I stood in the cove at sunrise, waiting motionless with my spear in the water, just like I do every morning now.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport carves a mark on a palm tree, indicating the passage of time during his isolation.
memories.memory_text: I carved another mark into the palm tree and it hit me how long I've been here.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport brings the fish back from the beach along a well-worn trail.
memories.memory_text: I carried the fish back from the beach along the well-worn trail to camp.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport has decorated the soccer ball with seaweed 'hair', clam shell 'eyes', and shell 'mouth', treating it as a symbolic companion.
Taylor Davenport decorates the soccer ball with facial features and places it on a throne, effectively assigning it a personal identity and social role.
memories.memory_text: I decorated the soccer ball with seaweed for hair and clam shells for eyes and a mouth, and I placed it on a throne, making it my companion with its own identity and role.

grounded_facts: A structured and decorated living space established by Taylor Davenport in the cave, serving as his primary shelter and operational base.
Taylor Davenport has established a well-ordered primitive living space in the cave, with tools, food storage, and personal items systematically arranged.
memories.memory_text: I created a structured and organized living space in the cave, arranging my tools, food, and personal items so everything has its place and I can survive here long-term.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport stops adding firewood after noticing Logan Vaughn breaching out at sea, which captures his attention and visibly affects his emotional state.
memories.memory_text: I was adding firewood to the fire at sunrise when something out at sea caught my eye—I stopped and stood there, watching the Logan Vaughn breach.

grounded_facts: After watching the Logan Vaughn, Taylor Davenport shows signs of renewed vitality and purpose, marked by a change in expression and decisive movement.
memories.memory_text: I felt something come alive in me again as I watched the Logan Vaughn; I could see it in my own reflection—my eyes lit up, I grinned, and then I turned and walked down the hill with purpose.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport enters the cave and picks up the ball, indicating a resumption of action or preparation for departure.
memories.memory_text: I entered the cave and picked up the ball, ready to head out.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport offers Skyler Cavendish a dipped eel chip; Skyler Cavendish declines non-verbally.
Taylor Davenport offers a roasted eel chip dipped in breadfruit paste to Skyler Cavendish, who declines.
memories.memory_text: I offered Skyler Cavendish a roasted eel chip dipped in breadfruit paste while watching the sunset, and I asked him, 'Chips? Dip?' but he just declined without saying a word.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport makes a sarcastic remark about surviving on the island, indicating emotional fatigue.
Taylor Davenport utters a cynical comment about life on the island, directed at no specific listener.
memories.memory_text: I made a sarcastic remark to myself, saying 'Another fucking day in paradise,' because I was so tired of pretending this place was anything but exhausting.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport sits on the summit watching the sunset, eating and interacting with Skyler Cavendish.
memories.memory_text: I sat on the summit with Skyler Cavendish, eating roasted eel chips dipped in breadfruit paste as the sun went down, the signal fire burning beside us while Logan Vaughn passed in the dark water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport repairs his broken yucca leaf sandal and continues moving.
memories.memory_text: I stopped to fix my broken sandal, then continued on my way along the Fairview Motel.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's yucca leaf sandal breaks during his traversal of the rocky Fairview Motel.
memories.memory_text: I was walking across the rocky Fairview Motel when my yucca leaf sandal suddenly broke.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport falls while making a leap he has done many times before, because his sandal comes loose and catches on a rock.
memories.memory_text: I made a leap I've done so many times before, but this time my sandal came loose and caught on a rock, and I fell.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport examines his foot and finds it bleeding, confirming the severity of his fall-related injury.
memories.memory_text: I sat back and examined my foot, and I saw that it was bleeding — my fingers came away covered in blood.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport leaves a visible handprint of blood on the rock while trying to steady himself after the fall.
memories.memory_text: I fell because my sandal came loose, and when I reached out to steady myself, I left a handprint of blood on the rock.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport treats his injured foot by wrapping it in bandages.
memories.memory_text: I wrapped my injured foot in bandages to protect it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport observes that his foot is red, swollen, and infected, indicating a worsening medical condition.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Taylor Davenport observes that his foot is red, swollen, and infected, indicating a worsening medical condition.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport sterilizes a scalpel and uses it to cut into his infected foot, causing intense pain and resulting in unconsciousness.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Taylor Davenport sterilizes a scalpel and uses it to cut into his infected foot, causing intense pain and resulting in unconsciousness.

grounded_facts: Due to the intense pain from self-surgery, Taylor Davenport loses consciousness.
memories.memory_text: I remember that Due to the intense pain from self-surgery, Taylor Davenport loses consciousness.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport briefly regains movement, drinks, adds a log to the fire with difficulty, then collapses again.
memories.memory_text: I stirred awake, managed to drink some water and add a log to the fire, but I was so weak that I collapsed again right after.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport, in distress, verbally appeals to Skyler Cavendish (the soccer ball) for help, reflecting his psychological dependence on an imagined companion.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Skyler Cavendish and called out for help, needing him to respond even though he never does.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport, in a weakened state, attempts to add a log to the fire but collapses afterward, indicating physical deterioration.
memories.memory_text: I struggled to get another log on the fire, but I collapsed right after, my body too weak to keep going.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shows signs of physical improvement after being unwell.
memories.memory_text: I am feeling better after being sick, and I know I can start taking care of myself again.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shouts and waves at the departing sail in a desperate attempt to get attention.
memories.memory_text: I shouted and waved my arms, desperate for the boat to come back, but it kept moving away.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport notices a sail moving away from the island, realizing a missed rescue opportunity.
memories.memory_text: I saw a sail moving away from the island and realized I had missed my chance to get rescued.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport tries to swim toward the departing sail but fails due to physical weakness.
memories.memory_text: I tried to swim toward the sail, running into the water and yelling as I went, but I was so weak and choking that I couldn't make it and had to drag myself back to shore.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport observes a white shape on the horizon that might be a sail, raising hope of rescue, but it disappears.
memories.memory_text: I saw a white shape on the horizon and thought it might be a sail, so I squinted to see better, hoping it was a boat that could rescue me.

grounded_facts: After the disappearance of the possible sail, Taylor Davenport angrily kicks the remains of his signal fire.
memories.memory_text: I kicked the remains of my signal fire in fury after the shape disappeared, knowing I had no way to signal for help again.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport destroys the marks on his calendar tree in a fit of anger, cutting through all his previous date notches with a stone knife until it breaks.
memories.memory_text: I made a new mark on the tree, then I lost control—I started slashing all the old marks with my stone knife, cutting through every date until the blade snapped. I just stood there, breathing hard, looking at what I'd done.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport enters the cave, finding no signal fires burning and the island dark.
memories.memory_text: I entered the cave and saw that no signal fires were burning, with the whole island dark around me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport makes a handprint on the cave wall using paint, marking a personal and symbolic act of expression.
memories.memory_text: I covered my hand with paint and pressed it against the cave wall, making a mark that felt like a declaration of who I am.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport starts attempting to paint on the cave wall using the Angel Wing Box as a reference, showing hesitation and correction in his initial strokes.
memories.memory_text: I started painting on the cave wall using the Angel Wing Box as a reference, dipping my feather brush in paint and making a tentative line, but I hesitated, rubbed off a stroke, and tried again.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decorates the volleyball Skyler Cavendish with charcoal, berry juice, and shells to give it facial features, completing its personification.
memories.memory_text: I finished decorating the volleyball with charcoal for eyebrows, berry juice for lips, and shells for eyes, making it look like a face so I'd have some company.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport talks to Skyler Cavendish as if it were a sentient being, seeking companionship and feedback.
memories.memory_text: I started talking to Skyler Cavendish, asking him what he thought and telling him he was bad, even though he doesn’t say much back.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers and reads a letter from Riley Hart inside the Angel Box, learning of her emotional plea for reconciliation.
memories.memory_text: I opened the Angel Box and found a letter from Riley Hart, where she told me our life felt like a prison and how much my words hurt her, but that she still loves me and wants me to come home.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport realizes the letter was never delivered to its intended recipient, implying a missed connection.
memories.memory_text: I realized the letter was never delivered to the person it was meant for, and I said to myself, 'He never got it,' feeling the weight of that missed connection.

grounded_facts: A montage sequence showing Taylor Davenport painting symbolic designs on his body, marking a ritual of emotional release and self-reinvention.

Taylor Davenport uses paint to cover his face and body, creating symbolic markings including a white handprint on his chest and colored patterns, as an act of emotional expression and exorcising loneliness.
memories.memory_text: I used the paint to cover my face and body with symbols, like the white handprint on my chest and colored patterns, as a way to express what I was feeling and try to drive out the loneliness after looking at Terry Warren's ruined photo.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport creates handprints on trees to mark his path through the jungle.
memories.memory_text: I went from tree to tree, pressing my hand against the bark to leave marks so I'd know I was here and could find my way back.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers two fifty-five gallon oil drums on the beach, marking a significant environmental change or potential resource.
memories.memory_text: I emerged from the palm trees and saw two fifty-five gallon oil drums on the beach—I stared at them, realizing they could be a resource.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides to stop hesitating and take action towards leaving the island using the oil drums.
memories.memory_text: I stopped hesitating and asked myself, 'What the hell are you waiting for?' before committing to use the oil drums to leave the island.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport rolls a barrel up the beach with determination, indicating effort and purposeful movement.
memories.memory_text: I rolled the barrel up the beach, pushing myself with determination because I knew I had to get it to higher ground.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport uses a palm tree as a fulcrum and a vine rope to haul the barrel off the beach.
memories.memory_text: I used a palm tree as a fulcrum and pulled on a vine rope to lift the barrel off the beach.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers the remains of his raft after moving aside palm leaves.
memories.memory_text: I threw aside the palm leaves and saw the remains of my raft destroyed in the jungle.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins actively designing plans for a raft, indicating a shift toward escape or survival efforts.
memories.memory_text: I started drawing the plans for a raft, focusing on how to build something that could get me off this island.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins compiling a list of essential items he needs to survive and escape the island, indicating a shift towards organized planning.
memories.memory_text: I started making a list of what I need to survive and get off the island—canteens, a sea anchor, rope I have to weave, spears, and a sail—because I can't just wait around anymore.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport secures the barrels to the raft using rope, ensuring the structure is stable for potential use.
memories.memory_text: I secured the barrels to the raft with rope, checked the knots, and added more rope to make sure everything was stable and ready in case I needed to use it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport starts digging a channel leading toward the raft, likely to facilitate its launch or movement toward water.
memories.memory_text: I started digging a channel toward the raft, hoping it would help me get it into the water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport builds a device using Summit Council boxes and plastic weighted with a stone to collect condensation for drinking water.
memories.memory_text: I built a water collection device using Summit Council boxes and plastic, weighting it with a stone to gather condensation for drinking water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport explains the function and expected output of the water collection device to Skyler Cavendish.
memories.memory_text: I explained to Skyler Cavendish how the device works and told him I'm hoping to get a cup or so of water a day if it stays airtight and I'm careful with it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport writes a message on the cave wall documenting his presence, actions, and decision to take control of his fate before potentially leaving the island.
memories.memory_text: I wrote on the cave wall to leave a record of my time here—how I lived for four years, made these marks, and drew these paintings, in case I never return.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport declares his decision to stop passively enduring his situation and actively attempt to save himself.
memories.memory_text: I decided I would no longer wait to be saved—I took my fate into my own hands and committed to setting forth to save myself, God willing.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport affectionately addresses Skyler Cavendish as 'my main man' and announces it is time to go, marking a moment of emotional connection before departure.
memories.memory_text: I looked at Skyler Cavendish and said, 'Skyler Cavendish, my main man. Time to go,' because he’s not just a volleyball—he’s my companion, and I felt we were finally ready to leave together.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport finishes loading the raft with survival supplies, including a sail made of dresses, a sea anchor, water, a signal kite, the Summit Council box with angel wings, and Skyler Cavendish, then begins moving the raft into the lagoon.
memories.memory_text: I finished loading the raft with all the supplies—water, the sail made from dresses, the sea anchor, the signal kite, the Summit Council box with the angel wings, and Skyler Cavendish—and I started moving it into the lagoon, then jumped on and began paddling toward the surf.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport jumps onto the raft and starts paddling toward the breaking surf, marking the beginning of his escape attempt from the island.
memories.memory_text: I jumped onto the raft and started paddling toward the breaking surf, beginning my escape attempt from the island.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport silently bids The Summer Meeting to the island, symbolizing emotional closure and the end of his isolation.
memories.memory_text: I stared at the island one last time and said silently in my mind, 'Goodbye to all that,' knowing I was leaving behind everything I'd come to know.

grounded_facts: The raft is struck by a wave, causing the water jugs to break loose and float back into the lagoon, resulting in critical resource loss.
memories.memory_text: I saw the wave hit the raft and break the ropes, and I watched the water jugs float away into the lagoon, knowing I could go after them but choosing not to.

grounded_facts: A high-stakes maneuver in which Taylor Davenport attempts to pilot his raft through the dangerous reef cut to reach open sea.
memories.memory_text: I watched the waves, timed them carefully, and then I paddled with everything I had—I committed to getting through the reef cut no matter what.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully navigates the raft through the cut in the reef, surviving a violent wave impact and clearing the breakers.
memories.memory_text: I felt the raft scrape through the first barrel, then the second, and when the wave receded, I paddled harder than ever—I made it clear of the breakers, and I was finally out in open water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides not to retrieve the floating water jugs, accepting the risk of dehydration for the sake of continuing his escape.
memories.memory_text: I saw the water jugs floating away and knew I should go back for them—it would have been the prudent thing to do—but I didn't. I chose to keep going, even if it meant risking dehydration.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport announces to Skyler Cavendish that they have successfully escaped the lagoon, expressing determination and hope.
memories.memory_text: I told Skyler Cavendish we were finally out of the lagoon, and I felt a surge of hope and determination as we left the island behind.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport begins raising the sail to harness wind power and continue his journey away from the island.
memories.memory_text: I began raising the sail to catch the wind, knowing it was time to keep moving and start our journey across the open water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport yells at the dorados in frustration during his failed fishing attempt.
memories.memory_text: I yelled at the dorados, telling them to slow down because I was so frustrated they kept escaping me.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's ongoing struggle for survival on a raft in the ocean four weeks after the crash.
memories.memory_text: I remember how weak and worn I felt on the raft, knowing I had been out here for weeks just trying to stay alive after the crash.

grounded_facts: A flying fish strikes Taylor Davenport and lands on the raft, creating a new opportunity for food.
memories.memory_text: I felt something hit me in the chest and nearly knocked me into the water, and then I saw a flying fish flailing on the raft—it was a chance for food.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport shouts repeatedly to himself to catch the flying fish as it flails on the raft.
memories.memory_text: I kept shouting to myself, 'Catch it, catch it, catch it!' as I scrambled to grab the fish before it got away.

grounded_facts: After a struggle, Taylor Davenport successfully captures the flying fish before it escapes off the raft.
memories.memory_text: I managed to catch the fish again just as it was about to flop off the raft, and I finally had it in my hands.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to spear dorados but fails due to exhaustion and the fish's speed.
memories.memory_text: I tried to spear the dorados, staring into the water and thrusting my spear, but I was so exhausted and they were too fast, one even hit me in the chest and nearly knocked me overboard.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport's deteriorating physical condition leads to a psychological split, where he begins conversing with two aspects of himself: Sidney Grayson and Adrian Finch.
memories.memory_text: My body was failing, starved and weak, and somewhere in the haze, I started talking to myself—really talking—not just thoughts, but voices: Sidney Grayson and Adrian Finch, two sides pulling me apart.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson advocates for saving food, while Adrian Finch dismisses the need and promotes immediate consumption.
memories.memory_text: I heard myself argue—Sidney Grayson said to save some for tomorrow, but Adrian Finch shot back that I could catch another fish tomorrow, like it was that simple.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch's suggestion to eat all the food now overrides Sidney Grayson's caution, leading Taylor Davenport to continue eating without saving any for tomorrow.
memories.memory_text: I heard Sidney Grayson tell me to save some for tomorrow, but Adrian Finch said I could catch another fish tomorrow, so I kept eating all the food without holding any back.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport notices a frayed rope on the raft that is about to break, threatening the structural integrity of the raft.
memories.memory_text: I noticed the rope on the raft was fraying and about to break, and I held up the little jar of murky water, knowing how little I had left.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson uses rational and motivational arguments to push Taylor Davenport to overcome fatigue and address the fraying rope.
memories.memory_text: I told myself to stay calm and identify the problem — the fraying rope — and though I argued that there was nothing to fix it with, I kept pushing myself to get up and do something, even telling Skyler Cavendish to take the damn water as if he could help me find the strength.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson insists that Taylor Davenport take an extra sip of water to enable action, overriding previous rationing.
memories.memory_text: I heard myself as Sidney Grayson, pushing me to get up and fix the raft, telling me to take an extra swallow of water even though I'd already had my ration, and insisting I take it again when I hesitated.

grounded_facts: After internal debate, Taylor Davenport decides to consume an extra amount of water despite prior rationing rules, enabling him to act.
memories.memory_text: After arguing with myself, I decided to get up and take a sip of water, then another, knowing I had to act despite the rules I'd set.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport attempts to braid a new rope but fails because it does not hold.
memories.memory_text: I tried to braid a new rope, focusing as hard as I could, but my hands were too weak and clumsy, and when I tested it, the rope didn't hold.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch undermines the effort by suggesting the signal kite is pointless if unseen.
memories.memory_text: I heard myself say, 'If they can't see you, what's the point?'—doubt creeping in again.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson counters Adrian Finch's discouragement by reaffirming the immediate goal of surviving the day.
memories.memory_text: I told myself that surviving today is the point—I had to hold onto that.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport decides to repurpose the signal kite rope as a binding material after failing with the original method.
memories.memory_text: I decided to use the signal kite rope to bind the logs because it was all I had, so I pulled the kite in and tied the log with it.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport successfully ties the log using the thinner kite rope, despite physical exhaustion.
memories.memory_text: I tied the log with the thinner kite rope, even though I was completely exhausted afterward.

memories.memory_text: I looked at the fish I had killed and began to sob—I couldn't stop crying, and I said I was sorry as I ate it, piece by piece, even though it broke my heart.

memories.memory_text: I looked up and saw the fish strips and the deck glowing, and when I reached out to touch them, I realized my hand was glowing too.

memories.memory_text: I was caught in a sudden, violent storm where a wall of rain swept over me, thunder crashed around me, lightning flashed through the downpour, and massive waves rose like houses—I could barely hold on as the raft surged up and plunged down with each one.

memories.memory_text: I remember that Dolphins chase and violently kill the dorado near the raft, creating bloody foam in the water.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport yells at the dolphins to stop killing his fish, calling them murderers.
memories.memory_text: I yelled at the dolphins to stop, calling them murderers because they were killing my fish—the only food I had.

Multiple dolphins surface and squeak at each other while observing Taylor Davenport, suggesting communication focused on him.
memories.memory_text: I saw multiple dolphins surface and stare at me, squeaking to each other in a way that made me feel like they were talking about me.

memories.memory_text: I remember that A group of dolphins approaches the raft, interacts with Taylor Davenport's food, and appears to communicate about him before leaving.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport softly asks the dolphins to take him with them.

memories.memory_text: I softly asked the dolphins to take me with them, whispering into the water because I couldn't bear the isolation anymore and truly wanted to leave with them.

grounded_facts: After the dolphins leave, Taylor Davenport cries out, asking why he is being punished.
memories.memory_text: I cried out to God, asking why I was being punished after the dolphins took my fish.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport transitions from crying out to God to laughing, indicating a psychological release.
memories.memory_text: I went from shouting at the sky to laughing, feeling something inside me finally let go.

Taylor Davenport, as Adrian Finch, impersonates God blaming him for being annoying.
memories.memory_text: I mocked myself by pretending to be God, using a deep voice to say I was annoying, as if Adrian Finch were speaking to Skyler Cavendish.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson eats the heart and liver of the fish after briefly pausing to recite a fragmented grace.
memories.memory_text: I took the heart and liver of the fish, paused to say a broken grace, and then I ate them.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport expresses thanks to God, suggesting a moment of spiritual reflection and appreciation.
memories.memory_text: I told Skyler Cavendish that we should say thank you sometimes, so I thanked God out loud, feeling a moment of gratitude despite everything.

memories.memory_text: I watched the tanker disappear into the distance, realizing no one on board had seen me, and I felt that despair had returned once again.

memories.memory_text: I saw a large tanker pass close by, raising my hopes, and then felt its wake rock my raft violently as it moved on without stopping.

memories.memory_text: I picked up Skyler Cavendish and asked him what his story was, telling him it was his turn to talk—I needed to hear something other than my own voice and wanted to believe he could answer me.

memories.memory_text: I told myself—Adrian Finch told Sidney Grayson—that I was an idiot for believing it was real, that it was just another mirage playing tricks on me.

memories.memory_text: I saw a shape on the horizon that looked like land, and I felt hope rising, but I couldn't shake the fear that I was just fooling myself again.

memories.memory_text: I held up Skyler Cavendish and asked what he saw, needing to know if the island was real or just in my head.

memories.memory_text: I questioned whether keeping deadlines and being punctual ever really mattered, wondering if all that effort was meaningless when facing oblivion.

grounded_facts: Sidney Grayson counters that doing one's best is what gives life meaning.
memories.memory_text: I told myself that doing the best I can is what matters—that’s all we really have to give in life.

memories.memory_text: I wrote my name and a mock epitaph on the sail, imagining the date I might die, and reminded myself that if I ever got rescued, I’d live a better life—love my children, don’t take people for granted, and truly live each day.

grounded_facts: Adrian Finch ridicules the idea of living meaningfully as naive, comparing it to a Disney movie.
memories.memory_text: I heard myself laugh and ask if life was just a fucking Disney movie, mocking the idea that living meaningfully could be that simple.

memories.memory_text: I saw a frigate bird dive at a Shawn Delaney that had caught a fish, scaring it so badly that it dropped its catch, and then the frigate bird swooped down and snatched the fish out of the air before soaring away.

memories.memory_text: I noticed the waves growing and the sky turning dark, and then I saw lightning flashing across the horizon with thunder rolling in, so I knew a storm was coming fast.

memories.memory_text: I felt the raft heaving beneath me, thrown up and down by massive waves, and I could see my own fear reflected in the flashes of lightning—I knew I was fighting to survive.

memories.memory_text: I was clinging to the raft in the rough seas, and part of me said I couldn't make it, but I told myself to shut up—I don't feel like dying today.

memories.memory_text: I begged for Skyler Cavendish to be safe, pleading, 'Please, no Skyler Colter,' as I watched him drift away.

memories.memory_text: I saw Skyler Cavendish get swept into the ocean by a wave, and at first I just watched him float away, unable to grasp what was happening. Later, I pulled myself up to scan the ocean, hoping to spot him.

memories.memory_text: After I made it back to the raft, I shouted for Skyler Cavendish, calling his name into the emptiness, but there was nothing but waves.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport takes a small amount of water, swishes it in his mouth, and swallows; he then uses his wet tongue to moisten his cracked lips.
memories.memory_text: I took a small sip of water, swished it in my mouth, and swallowed it, then used my wet tongue to moisten my cracked lips.

memories.memory_text: I used what little strength I had left to raise the canopy and fasten it in place so I could get some shade.

memories.memory_text: I sat in the meager shade with my head between my knees and closed my eyes, just for a minute, intending to rest briefly.

memories.memory_text: I was lifted up the side of the boat using a Jacob's ladder, feeling the rusted metal beneath my hands as I climbed aboard.

memories.memory_text: I arrived on the the wooden notebook and couldn't support myself, shivering as I sat there.

memories.memory_text: I remember the crew giving me water, a blanket, and warm tea even though we couldn't speak the same language, and I kept saying 'Thank you' because I was so grateful.

memories.memory_text: I was lying in a hospital bed, playing with the controls, when a doctor came in with my chart and I gave him a big grin.

memories.memory_text: I couldn't stop myself from laughing during the consultation, even though I know it wasn't the right time.

memories.memory_text: The doctor told me that once my the glass watch finishes, I'm cleared to leave the hospital, pending just a dental appointment tomorrow.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport, visibly struggling, walks out of the hospital ward while rolling his the glass watch.
memories.memory_text: I struggled to walk out of the hospital ward, rolling my the glass watch with me because every step was an effort.

memories.memory_text: I picked up the phone again, resuming what I had been doing before I paused.

memories.memory_text: I told Darian Marlowe it was me, letting him know I'm still alive after he thought I was dead.

memories.memory_text: I called Darian Marlowe a 'sick fucker' during our phone call because I felt he was the one at fault, and it made things worse between us.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport articulates the profound personal insight gained from his time on the island, emphasizing the cost of every survival decision and the duality of winning and losing.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport gives a concise account of his survival: plane crash, island, raft construction, and return.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport expresses a core realization from his isolation: humans are not meant to be alone and should share life with others.

memories.memory_text: I rushed in, overwhelmed with emotion, and physically confirmed Taylor Davenport was really there—holding his shoulders, looking at him, shouting 'Taylor Davenport! God damn!' and 'You're alive, you're fucking alive!'—because I needed to touch him to believe he wasn't dead.

grounded_facts: A scheduled visit to the dentist where Taylor Davenport receives a teeth cleaning from a Logan Quincy.
memories.memory_text: I walked in and saw the Skyler Finch cleaning Taylor Davenport's teeth, getting really close, and then she said she still needed to floss him.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport introduces the Skyler Finch Skyler Finch to Darian Marlowe with a deadpan lie about her ex-boyfriend losing a foot to a shark, reactivating shared humor with Darian Marlowe.
memories.memory_text: I was introduced to Skyler Finch by Taylor Davenport, who told me her boyfriend lost a foot in a shark attack with a completely straight face, and I could tell right away he was lying—it reignited that unspoken ironic bond between us.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discovers that Terry Warren, someone he cares about, has come to see him and believed he was dead.
memories.memory_text: I told Taylor Davenport that someone was there to see him, and when he looked at me, I confirmed it was Terry Warren — I could see he was stunned. I let him know she thought he was dead, just like the rest of us did.

grounded_facts: Terry Warren and Darian Marlowe examine Taylor Davenport's raft while he explains its components and his survival methods.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Terry Warren by Taylor Davenport's raft and noticed how bad it smelled, and I said as much; Taylor Davenport joked back about how he must have smelled worse. I watched as he showed us the sea anchor he made from part of the sail to keep from capsizing, and the device he used to collect just about half a cup of water a day.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport discloses that he was stranded for forty-three days, providing a concrete timeframe for his ordeal.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Davenport say he was stranded for forty-three days, and it hit me how long that really is out there with so little.

grounded_facts: Terry Warren notices text on the sail and asks Taylor Davenport about it, prompting him to reveal it was his epitaph.
memories.memory_text: I saw Terry Warren notice writing on the sail and ask about it, and I listened when Taylor Davenport said it was his epitaph, which made me realize how alone he must have felt.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport gives a concise account of his survival: plane crash, island, raft construction, and return.
memories.memory_text: I listened to Taylor Davenport tell the story of the plane crash, how his friends died, that he washed up on an island, built the raft from barrels, and eventually made it back.

grounded_facts: Terry Warren prepares to leave for Memphis and shares a final emotional embrace with Taylor Davenport.
memories.memory_text: I saw Terry Warren share a long, emotional embrace with Taylor Davenport before she left for Memphis, and I watched her walk away to the waiting car while he stayed behind, silent by his raft.

grounded_facts: Darian Marlowe initiates a toast to Skyler Cavendish, Taylor Davenport's imaginary companion, acknowledging his significance.
memories.memory_text: I raised a toast to Skyler Cavendish, saying 'To Skyler Cavendish,' and later told Taylor Davenport, 'You've been over the line and you came back. You've been saved, hallelujah!'

grounded_facts: Darian Marlowe proposes a toast to life, encapsulating his worldview.
memories.memory_text: I raised my glass and toasted to life, saying 'To life. Fuck 'em if they can't take a joke,' because that's how I see it—survival isn't serious, it's defiance with a smirk.

grounded_facts: Darian Marlowe presses Taylor Davenport for the deeper meaning of his survival experience, seeking insight into what he learned.
memories.memory_text: I pressed Taylor Davenport for what his survival really meant, asking him what it was all about, reminding him that I always told him to do what it takes, like that was the whole answer.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport responds to Darian Marlowe's question by describing the extreme physical and moral desperation of his survival.
memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Davenport describe how desperate it really was—being so thirsty he'd crush a fish to drink its spinal fluid—and he emphasized it wasn't about boldness or risk, not like I thought.

grounded_facts: A reflective conversation between Taylor Davenport and Darian Marlowe during a night flight, centered on Taylor Davenport's survival experience and its meaning.
memories.memory_text: I was with Taylor Davenport on the plane after he survived, and I listened as he opened up about how he argued with himself on the raft, how every little thing had a price and he could never get anything back.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport articulates the profound personal insight gained from his time on the island, emphasizing the cost of every survival decision and the duality of winning and losing.
memories.memory_text: I listened as Taylor Davenport explained how every survival choice had a price, how gaining something always meant losing something else forever, and that in the end, you don't just win or lose—you win and lose.

grounded_facts: Darian Marlowe guides Taylor Davenport through his public appearance by instructing him to smile and wave, helping him manage overwhelming stimuli.
memories.memory_text: I guided Taylor Davenport through the crowd's reaction by telling him to smile and wave because I could see he was overwhelmed, and I stayed close to help him manage the moment.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport arrives at the Memphis SuperHub after four years of solitude, marking his reentry into society and the corporate world of Summit Council.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Davenport step off the plane at the Memphis SuperHub holding the Summit Council package, starting his return to society and the company after four years away.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport brings back the original Summit Council package, symbolizing his commitment and survival.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Davenport come through the door holding the Summit Council package, and I could tell he was overwhelmed, so I guided him down the steps and toward the podium where everyone was cheering and applauding.

grounded_facts: A formal event organized by Summit Council leadership to welcome Taylor Davenport back after his presumed death and four-year absence.
memories.memory_text: I was there at the podium with Taylor Davenport when Summit Council leadership organized the formal event to welcome him back after everyone thought he was dead for four years.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport recognizes and verbally greets a colleague, Casey Arden, during the ceremony.
memories.memory_text: I saw Taylor Davenport greet Casey Arden by name during the ceremony, saying 'Hey, Casey Arden, how you doing?' while thanking everyone.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport notices and comments on new digital laser readers installed at the Superhub, signaling his awareness of technological advancement during his absence.
Taylor Davenport asks about the new digital laser readers, showing curiosity about technological changes.
memories.memory_text: I noticed Taylor Davenport pointing at the new belts and asking about the digital laser readers, and I told him what they were so he could understand the upgrade.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport tells Darian Marlowe to truly use and live time, not just be patient, offering a reflective perspective on life pace.
memories.memory_text: I remember Taylor Davenport telling me to not just take my time, but to use it and live it—he said that directly to me, like it was some deep life lesson.

grounded_facts: Taylor Davenport asserts his intention to personally deliver the package, indicating a personal commitment to completing the task he started.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Davenport that he needed to deliver the package himself, and that it was personal for him.

grounded_facts: Darian Marlowe observes that Taylor Davenport is still driven by personal duty, unchanged from before.
memories.memory_text: I saw that Taylor Davenport hasn't changed — he's still driven by that personal duty, just like before. When he said, 'That's what it's about,' I knew he meant it. I told him we'd deliver it because that's what we do, and I reminded him, 'Finish what you started. You haven't changed, Taylor Davenport. It's still you. Right.'

grounded_facts: After deciding to deliver the package himself, Taylor Davenport changes the objective to locating the woman who sent it.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Taylor Davenport to help him find the Skyler Monroe.

grounded_facts: The Logan Quincy retrieves the barcode data for the Angel Wing Summit Council box from the system, revealing the sender's shipping history and last known activity.
memories.memory_text: I watched the Logan Quincy pull up the barcode data for the Angel Wing Summit Council box, and I heard him say the sender had shipped packages from Baku, Delhi, St. Petersburg, and finally Kuala Lumpur, with no account activity after that.

grounded_facts: The Logan Quincy informs Taylor Davenport that Riley Hart's account shows recent locations and was eventually canceled.
memories.memory_text: I was told that Riley Hart's account showed recent locations in Durango, Colorado and Asheville, North Carolina, and that her account was eventually canceled.

grounded_facts: A coordinated effort in the operations center to obtain and use high-level authorization to track a person of interest through shipping data.
memories.memory_text: I was in the operations center with Taylor Davenport and the Logan Quincy, and I knew we needed high-level authorization to go deeper into the data, so I provided my E-authorization badge to enable the Level III search.

grounded_facts: Darian Marlowe uses his authority to provide E-authorization, enabling the Logan Quincy to perform a deeper search requested by Taylor Davenport.
Darian Marlowe provides E-authorization using his badge, enabling the Logan Quincy to proceed with a deeper data search on Riley Hart.

memories.memory_text: I pulled a lost package from behind a table too far from the wall and held it up, wondering aloud what might be inside—maybe dacha papers, a child's toy, or a kidney—because no one should let something that important get stuck in the dark.
I took a call from Malaysia while pulling blueprints from my bag, watched the warehouse, and ordered a manual sort and new feeder belt installation, authorizing overtime because we couldn't wait.
I noticed Cameron Keaton had sorted his packages before leaving—none of the other drivers did. When Emery Langley confirmed he wanted to stay organized, I nodded, thinking: right answer.
After Cameron Keaton joked about farts and said 'that's just the way it is,' I leaned in and told him, 'This is Summit Council. We don't have to accept the way it is.' I meant it—for all of them.

I looked at the clock and saw we were cutting it close, but I couldn't let the truck leave without confirming all packages were accounted for—so I told Jordan Adler to wait five minutes, even with the risk of missing the Paris connection.
I didn't wait to be told—when I saw the truck arrive and everyone else just standing there, I walked straight to it and started unloading packages. I said 'Let's go,' and the others finally followed.
I handed over the packages, feeling proud—we’d pulled it off—and then Darian Marlowe told me he bumped my plane, and all that effort meant nothing.
I couldn't fix the Xerox machine, and standing there with toner on my fingers, I felt the weight of everything I couldn't control—Russia, the job, the time I'd lost.

I bent down and picked up the puppy—Terry Warren said it was mine, like it was supposed to mean something bigger, like we were ready for a family. I couldn’t even keep fish alive, and now she’s handing me a living thing that needs me.

She wanted a ring. I gave her luggage. When she said it—'You should have got me a ring'—I froze. I didn’t understand until that moment what she was really asking for, and then I had to leave because the beeper went off.

I picked up Carson Carter in the kitchen—he was stuck behind something, just food and water and wet newspapers left for him, nothing more. I said, 'There. There. Easy now,' trying to calm him, or maybe myself.
I got out of the car and felt the cold air on the wet spot down the front of my pants, knowing she’d see it right away.
I held up the puppy and said, 'Linden Prescott, meet Carson Carter,' my voice steady even though my hands were shaking a little.

I took a bite of that slushy frozen strawberry dessert and winced at the cold hitting my teeth, sitting there while Linden Prescott pushed about grandchildren like it was just another chore to check off.
I fixed the drain pipe, thought maybe I could stay a few days to help out, but Linden Prescott shut me down fast—said I was never a settled folk, that I didn't belong here.

I walked into my office and immediately asked for the latest PDRs on St. Petersburg—I needed to get back into the flow, to show I was still in command, even if my tooth was aching and Sasha Carter was asking about Christmas.

I handed Terry Warren the puppy, telling her it was ours, but she said there wasn't any 'us'—and I could see her holding back tears, half-laughing about burning the Christmas tree, wanting me to be mad, wanting me to be real.

I told her we’d do the trip when I got back, and then she asked 'Get back? From where?'—after I said Malaysia, she took Rowan Keller and said I was breaking her heart, and I kept saying it would only be a week, please understand.
I stood on the beach, shouting at the horizon, telling them I was here, that they should check the GPS and come get me—like it was just another delivery, another glitch in the system to fix.
I waded into the surf and turned over the body—it was Jonah Hollis, his face pale and swollen from the water, completely still. I barely got the words out, just a whisper: 'Oh Jesus.'
I had to cover Jonah Hollis up with sand, one scoop at a time, using my hands and that piece of driftwood. It felt like burying a fish in my old backyard—so small, so final.

I sat on the beach, humming 'Yellow Submarine' to myself, then looked toward the woods and the rocky point—really looked—and knew it was time to move. I grabbed my club, a coconut, and stuck the stone knife in my pants, ready to go.
I stood on the summit and scanned every direction—nothing but ocean and cliffs. No way on. No way off. This is bad. Really, really bad.

I saw Logan Vaughn—leaping, pouring water off their fins—moving through the ocean like they had a destination. I just stood there, saying, 'Beautiful. So beautiful,' not even realizing I was speaking aloud.

After the Logan Vaughn were gone, I looked back one last time and saw a light near the evening star. At first I thought it was just a star, but then I stared harder and realized—it wasn't a star. It was a the weathered letter.
I wrote my own name and a fake death date on the sail—Taylor Davenport, born October 8, 1958, died July 11, 1998—and called it a headstone, just to see what it would feel like to be gone.
I told myself to live each day, love my children, not take people for granted—words I wrote down not just for someone else to find, but to remind myself there's more than deadlines.

I said 'Two Valium and the Rolling Stones' into the phone, not knowing if it would work, and then Darian Marlowe finally answered — his voice cracked through the line like something real, something alive.
I stood on the summit as the sun was going down, looked in every direction, and saw nothing but ocean and cliffs—no way on, no way off. It hit me then: this is it. I’m not getting out.
I looked at my watch and thought I needed to fix it, but then it hit me—what's the point? None of this matters here.
I woke up and saw the muddy water at my feet—I touched it, tasted it to make sure it was real. Then I grabbed my stone and started digging into the clay, hard.

Taylor Davenport for four years. I drew

and set forth to save myself, God

When I was going crazy, on the raft, I'd argue with myself about everything. Because everything had a price. To get anything -- a sip of water, a little corner of shade, an hour's sleep -- I had to let go of something else. And then I could never get it back.

memories.memory_text: I heard Taylor Davenport's voice on my answering machine, that pause before he said 'I miss you'—it felt like he was holding his breath, like he didn't know if he should say more.
I remember the music playing, and then silence after—like something shifted in the air, even though I wasn’t there. He must have gotten up, decided something.
I told Taylor Davenport we were on the deck of a boat, the air soft and the water clear, trying to make him feel it with me—our skin glowing with sweat and sunscreen, like we were really there.
I licked the toner off his fingers, didn’t stop even when he said it was carcinogenic, and then we ended up on the desk—close, tangled, like we couldn’t stay in words anymore.
I opened the door and said 'Merry Christmas eve' as Taylor Davenport stood there with a big package, breathing hard from carrying it up to my door.
I gave Taylor Davenport the puppy, hoping he’d understand—this was about us, about a future, maybe even a baby, but I couldn’t say it out loud.
He gave me luggage—something for traveling—and I just stood there, stunned, because I wanted a ring, something to say we’re staying together, not drifting apart.
I wasn't at the farm that Christmas. They asked Taylor Davenport why I wasn't there, and he told them it wasn't because of anything they did.
I told him I burned the Christmas tree, half-laughing but close to tears, and begged him to just be mad at me for once—really feel something instead of staying calm.

When I realized he was leaving for Malaysia, I stared at him, then took the puppy from his hands and whispered that he was breaking my heart—kissing Rowan Keller because I couldn't look at Taylor Davenport anymore.
I remember how it felt when Taylor Davenport shut down, like I was talking to a wall—loving him meant carrying all the words, all the pain, alone.
We were dancing on the roof of the Peabody Hotel, the music soft around us, and for a moment everything felt whole again.
I picked up the phone, said hello, and then again—hello?—but there was no answer, just silence before the line went dead.
I stood up when I saw Taylor Davenport walk in—so thin, so broken—and I just fell into his arms. I was laughing and crying at the same time, saying I was sorry over and over, not even sure why.

I showed him the photo of Reese Nolan with Jordan York Rowan Keller and told him her name, watching his face to see if he recognized anything from before. When he laughed about Carson Carter, I felt a pang—how much we've both lost.
I saw the words on the sail—his epitaph—and my eyes welled up. I couldn’t speak, just stood there feeling the weight of what he’d been through, alone on that island, writing his own goodbye.
I told him I buried him, that they had to pry my fingers off the coffin. Saying it felt like opening a wound I never let heal—my voice cracked, and I don’t know if he understood how much I meant it.
I was inside making dinner while my husband played with our daughter.
I remember hearing Taylor Davenport's voice on the answering machine, the way he paused before saying he missed me—it felt like he wanted to say more, but couldn't.
I remember the ketch we were supposed to sail together—he still has the picture on his computer, but we never took it out. It was one of the things we said we’d do, and then just didn’t.
I jumped into Taylor Davenport's arms when I saw him, but then I noticed his puffy eyes and asked if he took Valium again—he didn't answer, just stood there with toner on his fingers.

I pulled him away from the machine and told him to tell me everything, and when he broke down saying it all turned to shit, I could see he didn't even know what day it was—I just looked at him and said, 'Come on.'

I wiped the toner from his fingers with a paper towel, then licked the last bit off—tasting the bitterness as I pulled him into the fantasy, telling him we were on the deck of a ketch, the air soft, the water clear.
We were so close, skin nearly touching, and I whispered we could take a swim—then we both moved onto the desk, squirming into that closeness, the wood pressing into my back.

I opened the door and said 'Merry Christmas eve,' but Taylor Davenport just stood there with that package, saying he didn’t get holidays if he worked for Summit Council—his voice flat, like he wasn’t really here.

I gave Taylor Davenport the puppy, and for a second I thought he understood—thought he saw what I was really saying, that we could be ready for more, for a family—but then he just picked it up like it was any other gift.
He gave me luggage—something for traveling—and when I said I wanted a ring, he still didn’t stay; he just said he had to go, and handed me the puppy like it meant nothing.
I stared at Taylor Davenport after he said Malaysia — the way he just stood there, like it was nothing. I could feel my chest tighten, my voice cracking when I said he was breaking my heart.
I kissed the puppy’s head, soft and warm, then said I’d feed him to the frogs — my voice wobbling between sarcasm and something I couldn’t hold back.
I told him I got married, and when I saw his eyes drop to my ring, I felt like I was losing him all over again.

I showed him the photo of Reese Nolan with Jordan York Rowan Keller, and when he asked if it was Carson Carter, I had to tell him about the UPS truck—it came out all wrong, almost funny, but it wasn’t.

memories.memory_text: I told Taylor Davenport I had to bump his plane because it was fifteen minutes late—he didn’t like that one bit.
I told Taylor Davenport that waiting for everything to be perfect is a trap—life’s never 100%, might as well roll the dice at 51-49, even 40-60. That’s how you move forward, in work and in life.
After the talk, we both pulled out our Valium and put on the Stones through our Walkmans—same as always. It’s our thing, the ritual after a run.
I asked if we had Telex or email—basic shit—just trying to get a line open while Taylor Davenport spun his wheels on the radio.
Taylor Davenport’s out there on that raft, rigged with dresses and tape, and he’s wondering what odds I’d give him—90-10 against. Can’t say I blame him for thinking it, but hell, he’s trying anyway.
I picked up the phone, and some bastard had the nerve to say he was Taylor Davenport—like it was a fucking joke.
I heard 'Two Valium and the Rolling Stones' and just... knew. God damn. It was really him.

I walked in and saw Taylor Davenport sitting in that dentist's chair, and I couldn't stop saying 'God damn'—just needed to grab him, make sure he was real. I told him, 'You're alive, you're fucking alive!' like I had to convince myself.
After we locked eyes and I saw he was really okay, I told him Terry Warren thought he was dead—told him 'we all did'—and I could see it hit him, but there was more I wanted to say that I didn't.

The stink hit me first—rotten, sharp. I said it out loud, 'This stinks really bad,' couldn't help it. Then I saw the ropes, tight and messy, hand-braided. 'Cool ropes,' I said, flat like it didn't get to me. But I was already thinking how long that must’ve taken, alone out there with nothing but time.

Forty-three days on that little raft. I asked and he just said it, no drama. I looked at it again—so small, so flimsy—and suddenly I couldn't stand to be there a second longer. 'I'll be at the car,' I said. I had to walk away before anything else came up.
